_readme: All site forms post to Netlify Forms via window.tgSend (SiteNav.dc.html). Home (index.html), About, Team, Technology, Procurement, Projects, brand, 404 and the case studies have no form of their own; pages listed under project-cta.pages embed the ProjectCTA form.

assessment.branching: Only branching is the track chosen on the path screen; each track has its own fixed 8-question list asked in order. No per-answer branching. Every question is single-select; option keys shown as A/B/C/D.

completedLead.onFailure: Errors swallowed (.catch(() => {})); tgSend itself shows the global #tg-form-fail toast.

payload.Name: fName
payload.PDF report: only when PDF failed: 'Could not be generated; the visitor can download it from the results page.'
payload.Readiness survey: 'Completed' + (hadPartial ? '. They came back and finished after an earlier "NOT completed" email; this one has the full results.' : '.')
payload._subject: 'Assessment lead ' + S.ref + ': ' + name + (org ? ' · ' + org : '') + ' (' + tierName + ', ' + score + '/100)'

completedLead.transport: window.tgSend(payload, { files: [['report', pdfBlob, fileName]] }) → multipart POST '/'. PDF built with buildPdf(A, true); 15 s timeout, otherwise sent without PDF.

incompleteLead.fields: { 'form-name': 'assessment', 'bot-field': '' } + tgFields(payload) (fallback: name, email, organization, subject, details=JSON.stringify(payload)), URL-encoded

payload.Name: fName
payload.Readiness survey: 'NOT completed. Answered ' + answered + ' of ' + total + ' questions. No report was generated.'
payload.Reason: 'Left the page before finishing' | 'No activity for 10 minutes'

triggers: pagehide event → reason 'Left the page before finishing' (uses navigator.sendBeacon('/'))
10 minutes with no answer after intake → reason 'No activity for 10 minutes' (fetch '/', keepalive)

colors.priorityNote: [0] is the on-screen CSS colour (pColor, unused in template), [1] is pPdf used for the on-screen chip dot and in the PDF

scoring.dimensionStatus: p = Math.round(dm[n][0] / dm[n][1] * 100); p >= 75 ? 'STRONG' : p >= 40 ? 'DEVELOPING' : 'GAP'; bar width = Math.max(p, 3) + '%' (displayed pct also floored at 3)
scoring.gapSort: gaps.sort((a, b) => b.impact - a.impact || a.qi - b.qi)
scoring.gaps: else { r = q.recs[v] || q.recs[0]; gaps.push({ impact: q.w * (2 - v), qi, t: r[0], d: r[1], dim: q.dim, ans: o.l }) }
scoring.padding: If fewer than 3 plan items, append items from pad[] in order (priority 'NEXT STEP') until there are 3.
scoring.perQuestion: sc += v * q.w; mx += 2 * q.w  (only answered questions count)
scoring.plain: Each answer is worth 0, 1 or 2 points times the question weight (1 or 2). The score is the share of the maximum possible, rounded to 0–100. 65%+ is Premier, 35–64% Growth Ready, under 35% Foundation. Every answer below 2 becomes an action item; its impact is weight × (2 − value), so 4 = high, 2 = medium, 1 = worth doing. Each area (Space, Infrastructure, Funding, Program, Timeline & Scope) is STRONG at 75%+, DEVELOPING at 40–74%, GAP below 40%.
scoring.score: pct = mx ? sc / mx : 0; score = Math.round(pct * 100)
scoring.strengths: if (v >= 2) strengths.push({ t: q.strong, dimUp: q.dim.toUpperCase() })

stationsQuestionTemplate.note: Only one rec; any non-2 answer (i.e. 'Not sure yet', v=0) uses recs[0].
recs: Define the scope
Station count drives space, infrastructure, and budget. Settle it early so everything else can be sized around it.
stationsQuestionTemplate.text: How many gaming stations are you envisioning?

foundation.desc: You’re at the start of the journey, which is exactly the right time for structured guidance. The action plan below gives you the order of operations.
foundation.name: Foundation

growth.desc: Meaningful pieces are in place, with a few key areas to resolve before breaking ground. Close the gaps below in order and you can move efficiently.
growth.name: Growth Ready

premier.desc: The foundations are in place to move quickly. You have alignment, resources, and momentum. This is a build-ready situation, and the next step is locking scope.
premier.name: Premier

options.l: Yes, secured and ready for build-out

recs: Define your site criteria
Know what your concept requires before you tour. It narrows the search fast.
Evaluate before you sign
Spaces vary widely in what they can support, and it can swing build costs. Get finalists evaluated first.
commercial.text: Do you have a commercial space identified or under lease?

options.l: Yes, we know what it can support

recs: Get the site evaluated
Gaming venues place unusual demands on a building. Knowing the limits early avoids costly change orders.
Finish the site evaluation
Close the remaining checks before the layout is finalized.
commercial.text: Has the space been evaluated for power, cooling, and network?

recs: Set an investment range
A working range tells you which concept the numbers can support.
Plan a phased build
Open with a core layout and design for expansion from day one.

recs: Pressure-test the business model
Validate the model for your market before committing to a layout.
Define success for the space
For an amenity, set the goal first and design usage around it.

options.l: Within 6 months, we need to move fast

recs: Set a target opening
Work back from a date to set your lease, design, and ordering milestones.

Late changes are the most expensive kind. Finalize the design first.

recs: Secure a space
Partner sites can sometimes get you open faster than a build-out. Explore options before committing.
Plan around shared use
Shared rooms need a different design approach. Factor that in early.
community.text: Do you have a physical space available for the facility?

options.l: Grant funding or donor commitments are in place
Funding is the main barrier right now

recs: Get a scoped, phased budget
Know exactly what you’re raising for, and what a realistic first phase looks like.
Strengthen your funding ask
Funders want reach, outcomes, and a credible budget. Package all three.
community.text: How is your organization positioned to fund the facility?

options.l: Very limited, technology is a known gap

recs: Plan for ongoing technical support
Without in-house IT, the facility needs a support plan to stay running. Budget for it up front.
Plan to move beyond consumer-grade
Consumer equipment rarely holds up to a full room of players. Plan for an upgrade.

A small pilot builds the participation numbers funders ask for.
Start tracking outcomes
Participation and outcome data strengthen every funding conversation.

Local employers and civic groups often back youth and workforce programs. Start those conversations now.

What participants gain shapes both the space and the funding pitch.

Connecting play to real skills widens who participates and who funds you.

A date, even a rough one, puts funding, space, and partners in the right order.
Align with funding cycles
Award dates often set your real timeline. Plan around them.

forms.submitLogic: preventDefault; collect every INPUT/SELECT/TEXTAREA (skip submit/button/hidden) keyed by its <label> text (fallback aria-label, name, placeholder, 'Field'); email value also copied to _replyto. payload = { _subject: 'League lead: ' + Full name + (Organization ? ' · ' + Organization : ''), _template: 'table', _captcha: 'false', ...fields, Form: 'League', Page: location.href, Submitted: new Date().toLocaleString() }. window.tgSend maps it to Netlify fields: form-name='league', bot-field='', name (Full name), email (_replyto/Work email), organization, phone (none on this form), subject (_subject), page, details = every non-underscore key as 'Key: value' lines. On success window.tgTrackLead('league') fires gtag 'generate_lead', fbq 'Lead', lintrk conversion if configured; then state.sent = true.
